scientific_question: Do resident wetland birds move within familiar space so that the environmental state they experience is more stable than event-matched local availability?
priority_design: individual-resolved repeated homing events with one used point and paired time-matched random points

eligibility.taxa: King Rail primary; wetland birds for replication
required: used versus paired random point identity
water depth or another repeated environmental-state variable
preferred: coordinates for used and random points
multiple individuals with >=3 valid matched events
reject_if: only static one-time habitat summaries are available
used points cannot be linked to time-matched availability
preferred state window is tuned after seeing the state-retention result
one individual drives the population-level interpretation

primary_estimand: State Retention Index: temporal variance of used water depth relative to matched random pseudo-trajectories
secondary_estimand: environmental displacement of real used trajectories relative to matched pseudo-trajectories, conditional on geographic movement
later_extension: full hydrological-portfolio/HPI analysis only if a repeated spatial habitat surface can be reconstructed

interpretation.positive_sri: experienced state is temporally more stable than locally available habitat
interpretation.null_sri: space use does not stabilize environmental state beyond availability

no_rescue: do not redefine point matching, water-depth variable, or SRI after inspecting individual results
